title: Cajeta cross-reference index, v1
description: The compiler's resolved view of a source root, source-mapped so an IDE can tie it back to editor offsets. Produced by `cajeta --emit-xref=<path>`, and (in lint mode) per-buffer on the diagnostic channel. Consumers MUST reject an unknown `version.major`: a wrong resolution is worse than a missing one, so a reader that cannot understand the document must disable xref-backed features rather than guess.

major.description: Breaking-change gate. A reader that does not know this value must refuse the document.

minor.description: Additive changes only. A reader may ignore fields it does not know.

sourceRoot.description: The root all `file` paths are relative to.

declarations.description: Every declaring form in the source root.

inheritance.description: extends/implements edges, with the parent as a RESOLVED FQN. This is the relation cajetadoc's model cannot supply -- there, extends/implements are raw declared names as parsed.

references.description: Each use site and the declaration it binds to. Populated from Unit 2.

overrides.description: Each overriding method and the method it overrides, matched on signature. Populated from Unit 2.

calls.description: Each call site and the callee the compiler resolved it to. Populated from Unit 2.

sourceRef.description: A half-open source span. Line is 1-based; col is 0-based (the ANTLR convention the compiler already carries on every AST node).

owner.description: FQN of the declaring type, for members.

annotations.description: Applied annotations, as canonical FQNs where the annotation type resolves (dev.cajeta.unit.Test), and as written otherwise. NAMES ONLY -- argument values are deliberately not recorded. Absent when the declaration carries none.

signature.description: Human-readable signature, for methods and constructors.

overloadKey.description: Identifies ONE overload. This is the compiler's own canonical unlabeled signature (Method::toCanonical(false)) -- the same string whose FNV-1a hash the RTTI uses for dispatch. Two same-name, same-arity overloads MUST get different keys: if they collide, 'who calls f(int32)' returns f(String)'s callers and renaming one overload rewrites the other's call sites.

parent.description: RESOLVED FQN of the parent -- never the raw name as written in the source.

target.description: FQN of the declaration this use site binds to. For a method, the overloadKey.

from.description: FQN of the enclosing declaration the use site sits in.

callee.description: overloadKey of the STATICALLY resolved callee. Possible dynamic targets are derivable from the inheritance + overrides relations and are deliberately NOT guessed here.

virtual.description: True when dispatch is dynamic, so a consumer knows to widen `callee` by the override set.
